Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
The first collision is A with B:

\[
10+3t=40-t \Rightarrow t=\frac{15}{2}
\]

They meet at \(x=65/2\). After bouncing, A moves left at speed 3, B moves right at speed 1, and C is at \(x=65\) moving left at speed 2.

B and C then meet after

\[
\frac{65-65/2}{1+2}=\frac{65}{6}
\]

more seconds, at time

\[
\frac{15}{2}+\frac{65}{6}=\frac{55}{3}.
\]

At that same instant, A reaches \(x=0\) and falls off. B and C meet at \(x=130/3\); after bouncing, B moves left and C moves right.

C falls at

\[
\frac{55}{3}+\frac{100-130/3}{2}=\frac{140}{3},
\]

while B falls at

\[
\frac{55}{3}+\frac{130/3}{1}=\frac{185}{3}.
\]

So the last ant falls after \(\frac{185}{3}\) seconds.

ANSWER: 185/3
